content: The Fair Packaging and Labeling Act (FPLA) is a United States law that governs the labeling of numerous consumer products. It mandates that product labels must include the following information: The identity of the product. The name and location of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor. The net quantity of the contents, expressed in U.S. customary units. This law was enacted during the presidency of Lyndon B. Johnson in 1966 and became effective on July 1, 1967. A requirement for metric labeling was later introduced in 1992 and came into effect on February 14, 1994. The law is codified in the United States Code. Currently, there is significant momentum within the industry to amend the FPLA to permit metric-only labeling. This push is partly driven by a European Union deadline of January 1, 2010, which prohibits dual-unit product labeling. Amending the FPLA to allow metric-only labeling would enable manufacturers, including both importers and exporters, to avoid the substantial costs associated with the potential need to produce two separate types of packaging.
